summary: The finding's measured costs are gone. useAutomationCentre (Projects map per checkout, AutomationsSummary, useProjectAutomations) reads providers from the live per-environment config store. getUsageSummary sends one request with no getConfig preflight, and contract mismatches are recognised from the answer. The server memoizes resolveAvailableEditors by platform+PATH with a 5-minute TTL, so loadServerConfig no longer runs the PATH and bundle scan per call. All three landed in 60633eff3 (#710), which the Hub vendor pin 7bc39eec3 includes. The other loadServerConfig inputs are cached already (keybindings via Cache, providers and settings from refs), so not adding the optional assembled-config cache costs little. Two small ad hoc getConfig callers the finding named in passing are still there. Both are per click and low value. See the correction field.

evidence.note: providers = useEnvironmentServerConfig(environmentId)?.providers. bind() (93-136) makes no getConfig call and returns early when the connection client is unchanged. The old f1be4abc7 code called next.server.getConfig() on every bind.
The browser test pins the rule that providers come from the live config and never from a getConfig read.

The store reads the primary serverConfigAtom or the saved-environment runtime store. The saved env's onConfigUpdated keeps it current (environments/runtime/service.ts:1352-1359, 1581-1586). A hosted node switch clears the primary atom (hostedHub/environment.ts:54), so a previous node's providers cannot linger.

getUsageSummary checks only the caller's input.contractVersion and sends one serverGetUsageSummary request with signal support. isUsageContractRejection (usage/compatibility.ts:30-40) maps three answers to UsageContractMismatchError: a client decode error on contractVersion, the node's UsageReadError (its message getter returns detail = USAGE_UPDATE_MESSAGE, see contracts usage.ts:150-158 and UsageService.ts:935-939), and an unknown request tag. Covered by wsRpcClient.usage.test.ts.

resolveAvailableEditors caches the default process.env scan under the key platform+PATH with AVAILABLE_EDITORS_CACHE_TTL_MS = 5 min. Explicit env or darwin overrides bypass the cache. #716 (2f1a62260) later added more bundle-CLI paths, which makes the scan more expensive, but the cache still covers it. open.test.ts:754-757 tests cache hit and invalidation.
loadServerConfig still assembles the config per call, but every input is now cheap: keybindings.loadConfigState is Cache-backed (keybindings.ts:438,603) and resolveAvailableEditors() is a cache hit.

Residual: openInPreferredEditor, used by ChatMarkdown.tsx:454 on file-link clicks, still fetches the full primary config only to read availableEditors. That costs about 1 RTT plus decoding an 85-130 KB config per click. OpenInPicker, SettingsPanels and DiagnosticsPanel already read availableEditors from the store.

Residual: readDraftDefaults always calls getConfig and then readEffectiveProjectPreferences, one after the other. It runs in parallel with the context fetch (line 289-292). It duplicates readNewDraftDefaults (hooks/newDraftDefaults.ts:99-136), which uses the cached config outside hosted mode and remembered preferences.
useHandleNewThread keeps the deliberate fresh getConfig only for hosted targets, as the verifier's caveat requires.

fixDefects: No defects found in the implemented fixes.
implementationSketch: Optional low-value follow-ups. Neither is needed for the finding's measured costs. (1) In editorPreferences.ts openInPreferredEditor, take availableEditors from getServerConfig() (client-runtime rpc/serverState.ts:74), falling back to api.server.getConfig() only while the store is null. This removes about 1 RTT and the full config decode per markdown file-link click, and matches what OpenInPicker already does. Update ChatMarkdown.browser.tsx mocks if needed and add a unit test that a non-null store makes no getConfig call. (2) In agentHandoff.ts readDraftDefaults, replace the inline getConfig + readEffectiveProjectPreferences with readNewDraftDefaults({ api, environmentId: projectRef.environmentId, cachedConfig: readEnvironmentServerConfig(projectRef.environmentId), requireFreshConfig: nodeIdForHostedEnvironment(envId) !== null || isHostedHubMode(), projectId }). Then map config.settings.defaultAgentTokenMode and initialDraftModelSelection as today. This removes duplicate logic and saves 1 RTT per non-hosted handoff. Do not add a blanket lint guard against getConfig: the hosted fresh reads in newDraftDefaults/executeChatSendTurn and the connect-time fallback in environments/runtime/service.ts:1239 are deliberate.
decisionReason: Client-only read-path changes. Hosted fresh-read semantics stay as they are, so no auth, E2EE, Hub protocol or lifecycle ownership is touched.
correction: The auditor's DONE stands. One nuance: the proposal's 'read config from the store instead of getConfig RPCs' is not fully applied. editorPreferences.openInPreferredEditor is still a pure probe (it fetches the full config for one field per click), and agentHandoff duplicates the uncached version of readNewDraftDefaults. Both are per user action and outside the finding's expected-gain scope. They are low-value cleanup, not a reason to downgrade.
